articles.title: Building a Timestamp-Aware AI Learning Assistant for Video Lectures
articles.excerpt: our team worked on an AI-powered learning assistant designed specifically for video-based education. The idea came from a simple problem: students often use AI while watching lectures, but a normal AI…
articles.body: our team worked on an AI-powered learning assistant designed specifically for video-based education. The idea came from a simple problem: students often use AI while watching lectures, but a normal AI assistant can answer using information from parts of the lecture that the student has not even watched yet. That can break the learning flow. So we built BuildVerse AI Learning Assistant , a system that understands not only the lecture content, but also the student’s current progress in the video. The Problem Imagine a student is watching a 60-minute lecture and has currently reached minute 20. They ask an AI assistant a question. A normal Retrieval-Augmented Generation system may search the entire lecture transcript and retrieve an answer from minute 45.

articles.body: The bill for a property marketplace's viewing confirmations has several parts: message delivery, sender setup, receipt collection, and the evidence retained after a recipient opts out or an address bounces. The dominant storage term is repeated receipt payloads. In a deliberately hypothetical sizing exercise, 10,000 confirmations with 12 saved observations of 1,000 bytes each produce 120,000,000 bytes; retaining one 400-byte decision record per confirmation produces 4,000,000 bytes. These are design inputs, not measured provider payload sizes or a claim about the dominant term in the total invoice.

articles.body: In Python, a string ( str ) is an immutable sequence of Unicode characters used to store and represent text. 1. Creating Strings Strings in Python can be created using either single quotation marks or double quotation marks. We can also use triple quotes to create multiline strings. single = 'hello' double = "World" multi_line = """Triple quotes let us write strings that span multiple lines.""" 2. Indexing and Slicing Strings are zero-indexed, meaning the first character starts at index 0 . You can also use negative indexing to access characters from the end. The index -1 represents the last character.

articles.title: Logistics Login: How to Trace Passwordless Phone SMS OTP Resend Cooldown Decisions
articles.excerpt: Gate logistics phone login on suppression status, resend cooldowns, and server-owned attempt limits, then log why each SMS OTP request was admitted or blocked. A dispatch desk needs to distinguish an…
articles.body: Gate logistics phone login on suppression status, resend cooldowns, and server-owned attempt limits, then log why each SMS OTP request was admitted or blocked. A dispatch desk needs to distinguish an invalid recipient from a courier who tapped “resend” too soon. Those conditions need different responses. TL;DR: For passwordless phone login in Express and Node.js, keep send-code, verify-code, resend-code, and lockout states in your backend. Check suppression before delivery. Apply increasing cooldowns and daily caps across phone, IP, and device. Measure policy decisions separately from delivery evidence. An accepted request isn't proof of a completed login. The useful unit is a login challenge, tied to a delivery attempt.

articles.body: A fixed-price quote should answer three questions: what will I deliver, what will it cost, and when is payment due? Here is a worked example for a one-page site. Start with delivery cost Suppose your time costs $40 per hour, you estimate 8 hours, and you have $40 in direct expenses. Your estimated cost is $360. To target a 20% margin on the final price, divide by 0.80. That gives a quote of $450 before tax . Adding 20% to the cost gives $432, which is a 20% markup but only a 16.7% margin. Quote detail Amount Labor and direct expenses $360 Fixed project price $450 50% deposit $225 Balance due on delivery $225 These numbers are illustrative. Choose a deposit and payment milestone that match the way you deliver the work.

articles.title: Designing APIs for AI Agents: What Should Change, and What Should Stay?
articles.excerpt: Originally written by Lucas Suárez for EkLine. Some of your API's callers are now agents. One times out on a POST and sends it again without knowing whether the first one landed. Another accepts a def…
articles.body: Originally written by Lucas Suárez for EkLine . Some of your API's callers are now agents. One times out on a POST and sends it again without knowing whether the first one landed. Another accepts a default nobody told it about. A third gets an error written for a person, reads the prose, and guesses. The pressure that follows is "redesign the API for agents." That redesign touches developers who integrate by hand, the logs support debugs from, and your compatibility promises. You have to decide where to spend first. Our answer: fix the shared API first. Make its behavior explicit, make the effective values of each call visible, and write a recovery contract that says which errors to fix, which to wait out, and when to stop.

articles.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
articles.excerpt: NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) in…
articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders.

articles.body: Encapsulate Inc. This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments. Orbiting more than 200 miles (320 km) above Earth, the space station is a powerhouse of cutting-edge science that is unlocking discoveries not possible on Earth. Image credit: Encapsulate Inc.
